metadata.title: Kennedy Center board votes to immediately close venue for renovations

sources.news_title: Published 5 hours ago • United States • Updated 47 minutes ago
sources.text:
Sans son nom dessus, Donald Trump menace de ne pas rouvrir le Kennedy Center
Le conseil d'administration du Kennedy Center à Washington, largement acquis à Donald Trump, a voté sa fermeture immédiate mardi, quelques heures après qu'un juge fédéral a interdit d'inscrire sur ce haut lieu culturel une référence au président sans l'accord du Congrès.
Le conseil d'administration du Kennedy Center a voté mardi 15 septembre la fermeture immédiate de ce haut lieu culturel de Washington que Donald Trump, qui le tient sous sa coupe depuis 2025, menace de ne pas rouvrir s'il n'obtient pas d'y faire figurer son nom.
L'annonce de la fermeture, faite par le président américain lui-même sur sa plateforme Truth Social et doublée de sa mise en garde, est intervenue peu après qu'un juge fédéral a statué que le nom de Donald Trump ne pouvait pas être réinscrit sur l'imposant bâtiment blanc sans l'accord du Congrès.
La décision du conseil d'administration - qui lui est largement acquis - de fermer "immédiatement" l'institution culturelle a été "presque unanime" et se fonde sur des "raisons de sécurité", a écrit Donald Trump. Il a dans la foulée conditionné des travaux de rénovation à une décision de justice favorable en ultime ressort à ce que son nom soit affiché sur l'édifice. "Si la décision est négative, ce qu'elle ne devrait pas être, et n'est pas cassée par la Cour suprême américaine, la reconstruction et la rénovation du Kennedy Center n'auront pas lieu", a-t-il menacé.

Quelques heures plus tôt, à l'issue d'une audience en référé, le juge Christopher Cooper avait statué qu'il était "interdit à la défense d'inscrire 'Rénové et restauré par Donald Trump' sur le bâtiment principal". "Pour faire simple, la défense ne peut pas installer de référence au président Trump (...) au Kennedy Center sans l'accord du Congrès", avait-il tranché.
Des fidèles de Donald Trump dans le conseil d'administration
Donald Trump a pris le contrôle du Kennedy Center - baptisé en souvenir de l'ancien président démocrate assassiné John F. Kennedy - peu après son retour à la Maison Blanche en 2025 en plaçant largement des fidèles dans son conseil d'administration, avec la volonté de "le remettre dans le droit chemin" et la promesse d'une programmation "pas woke". Son nom avait été accolé à celui de JFK sur la façade en décembre dernier.
Mais une première décision du juge Cooper fin mai avait ordonné au conseil d'administration du Kennedy Center de retirer toute référence "au président Trump ou à tout individu autre que le président Kennedy" sur le bâtiment lui-même, son site internet et ses marques déposées. Le Kennedy Center avait annoncé en juin s'être exécuté.
Son conseil d'administration est toutefois revenu à la charge au cours de l'été avec un nouveau projet visant à rendre hommage, par une inscription sur l'édifice, à l'engagement de Donald Trump pour la rénovation de l'institution culturelle.
Ses membres arguent que, face à l'état précaire des finances du Kennedy Center et de son bâtiment, seul Donald Trump est en mesure de lever des fonds et de mettre sur pied une réhabilitation d'envergure, et qu'à ce titre il est légitime que son nom figure sur la salle de spectacle.
Des artistes boudent le Kennedy Center
Le juge Cooper y a de nouveau fait obstacle mardi. Dans sa décision de mai, ce même magistrat avait également suspendu à titre provisoire la fermeture pour deux ans de la salle, considérant que le conseil avait manqué à son "devoir de prudence" en ne tenant pas compte des retombées négatives de cette fermeture.
Il avait néanmoins autorisé la poursuite des travaux de réparation prévus au Kennedy Center, dont "le besoin apparaît criant" et précisé qu'il ne s'opposerait pas à une nouvelle décision de fermeture si elle était prise au terme d'une évaluation plus approfondie.
Depuis qu'elle est passée sous la coupe de Donald Trump, nombre d'artistes - par exemple, la très populaire comédie musicale "Hamilton sur la naissance de la démocratie américaine - boudent la salle de spectacle. Selon la presse américaine, les ventes de billets et les collectes de fonds se sont effondrées.
S'il ne s'est prononcé que sur sa fermeture, le conseil d'administration devait initialement examiner dix propositions visant à faire référence à Donald Trump, allant de variations autour de "rénovation et financement supervisés par le président Donald J. Trump et le fonds Trump Kennedy Center" à "un héritage préservé grâce à la générosité du président Donald J. Trump".
Avec AFP

Sept. 15 (UPI) — The board of the Kennedy Center for the Performing Center voted Tuesday to immediately close the center for renovations, hours after a federal judge ruled that President Donald Trump‘s name must stay off the building.
Trump said in a social media post that the closure was for “safety reasons” and so renovations can begin on the building. However, he also said the renovations will not start — and the center will not reopen — until his name is added to the center again.
“The Renovation and Reconstruction, which is a very large and complex job, cannot begin until such time as the D.C. Circuit rules on the Board’s approved name,” Trump wrote, referring to an ongoing lawsuit by Rep. Joyce Beatty which seeks to keep Trump’s name from the center named for the late President John F. Kennedy.
“If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and Renovation of the Kennedy Center will not take place,” Trump wrote.
Judge Christopher Cooper’s ruling Tuesday denied an attempt by the center’s board to return the president’s name to the building.
“Simply put, defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’ blessing,” Cooper said in his ruling.
The center’s board members — all of whom were named by Trump after he dismissed the previous board — said Monday that the center is facing bankruptcy and could close as soon as Tuesday.
They said the only way to save the center from closure was to add Trump’s name to the building and the president’s support in fundraising was contingent on “appropriate recognition.”
The Justice Department has also threatened to demolish the center if the Trump-ordered renovations do not take place.
Although Cooper ruled in May that Trump’s name must be removed from the center, the board voted in August to return the name, this time as part of a statement honoring Trump for proposed renovations. It would also rename the physical grounds “The President Donald J. Trump Plaza.”
Cooper said in his order Tuesday that the Justice Department provided “no proof that current or future donations hinge on President Trump’s being on the building” and “no competent proof that removing the Trump name would prevent the center from fulfilling its artistic mission.”
The board’s newest attempt “bucks a federal court order and a statute Congress enacted,” Cooper wrote in the ruling.
“And yet the drama at the Kennedy Center continues,” he wrote.
Before it can fully shut the center down, the board will need to get a ruling reversing Cooper’s earlier order requiring that the center stay open while the lawsuit over the name continues.
The board — which elected Trump chairman — first renamed the center to add Trump’s name in December. The president said the name change was a surprise, but his name was added to the center the next day.
A number of artists and shows that were set to appear at the center canceled after Trump’s name was added to the building, while others said they would no longer accept invitations to perform there.
Although the board eventually removed Trump’s name from the building in June — at the very end of the court-ordered deadline — tarps and scaffolding at the site still block the view of the center’s name. In late June, Cooper requested an explanation for their presence.
In a filing in August, the Kennedy Center lawyers said the scaffolding and tarps remained the facilitate renovation work on the soffits, or eaves, of the building.
In a response, Beatty,o who led the lawsuit against the Kennedy Center renaming, said the explanation for the remaining scaffolding and tarps “falls apart under scrutiny.”
“The soffits are some 20 feet or more above the scaffolding,” her response reads.
She said that the fact that the center has only left up the scaffolding obscuring the name of the building is “a strong indication that this structure has nothing to do with the roof and is, instead, meant to defy a return to the status quo.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. — The board of the Robert F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts voted to close the center’s main building immediately for renovations on Tuesday, just after a federal judge blocked the board’s latest attempt to add President Donald Trump’s name to the building.
Board members argued the center’s deteriorating physical shape required the closure, with a draft board resolution noting an incident earlier this month in which a 5-foot-long section of plaster fell from the ceiling of the center’s Grand Foyer during a storm. Trump posted on social media that the center was “in a virtual state of collapse.”
Board members also noted a “dire” financial position in which the center would face “certain fiscal collapse within weeks.” Since the board initially voted to add Trump’s name to the building in Dec. 2025, the center has seen plummeting ticket sales and canceled performances. It has had virtually no public performances since July.
Tuesday was the third time the board voted for a two-year closure for repairs since February.
Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, an ex officio board member, has challenged those efforts in court. Ahead of the vote, her attorneys said an earlier ruling already prevents the board from fully closing the center during repairs.
“The court has ordered the Kennedy Center to remain open pending further decision of the court, so that vote today will not be able to close the Kennedy Center,” said Norm Eisen, co-founder and executive chair of Democracy Defenders Fund, the group representing Beatty in court.
The vote came about an hour after a federal judge again ruled that Trump’s name could not be added to the building’s façade, writing that doing so would violate his previous ruling from May: “Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing.”
The center’s board had prepared a separate resolution to restore the president’s name to the building, arguing that it would be the only way to ensure his continued support—and fundraising abilities, even though Congress has already allocated $257 million for renovations.
The president confirmed that his involvement was contingent on his name being added to the center when he posted on Tuesday that renovations would not begin until a court approves the center’s name change.
Beatty said she would continue to challenge the closure and name change in court.
“We want to make sure that we keep the Kennedy Center healthy,” she said. “And certainly, as you know, we have been dealing with the unlawful naming, and it is being held hostage.”
The Kennedy Center did not respond to a request for comment.
